reading_levels.student: TFEB-driven expansion of the lysosomal compartment.
reading_levels.research: The return arm of the lysosome-to-nucleus circuit (SET2012): mTORC1 phosphorylation keeps TFEB out of the nucleus, and when it is released TFEB expands the very organelle on which mTORC1 is regulated. This closes a genuine homeostatic loop that a linear diagram cannot show.

studies.title: A gene network regulating lysosomal biogenesis and function
studies.authors: Sardiello M; Palmieri M; di Ronza A; Medina DL; Valenza M; Gennarino VA; Di Malta C; Donaudy F; Embrione V; Polishchuk RS; Banfi S; Parenti G; Cattaneo E; Ballabio A

studies.model_system: Promoter/expression analysis of lysosomal genes; cultured human (HeLa) and mouse cells with TFEB overexpression; lysosomal storage conditions (sucrose loading)
studies.finding: The authors found that most lysosomal genes show coordinated expression and share a promoter motif (later called the CLEAR element) that is bound and regulated by the transcription factor TFEB. Under conditions of abnormal lysosomal storage, TFEB moved from the cytoplasm to the nucleus and switched on its target genes. Overexpressing TFEB in cultured cells increased the number of lysosomes and the cells' capacity to degrade complex molecules, including glycosaminoglycans and the mutant huntingtin protein. The paper provided evidence that lysosome production is run by a transcriptional programme with TFEB at its centre, which later work tied to mTORC1 control. Boundary: Cultured cells with TFEB overexpression; mTOR was not studied in this paper. Therapeutic potential for storage and neurodegenerative disease is proposed, not tested. Drafted from the abstract only (no PMC full text).

relations.mechanism: Nuclear TFEB switches on the lysosomal and autophagy gene programme as a single coordinated module, expanding the lysosomal compartment.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In the nucleus, TFEB switches on a whole gene package for cleanup and for building new lysosomes.
relations.boundary: Transcriptional output measured as gene expression and lysosomal markers; how much the compartment actually expands varies with cell type and starvation depth.

relations.mechanism: A larger, renewed lysosomal compartment changes the platform on which mTORC1 is regulated – the return leg of the lysosome-to-nucleus circuit.
relations.mechanism_beginner: More, fresher lysosomes change the very platform that controls mTORC1 – closing a loop back to where the signal started.
relations.boundary: SET2012 establishes lysosome-to-nucleus signalling via mTOR and TFEB; the quantitative effect of compartment size on mTORC1 output is not resolved.
